headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: MinerU can read local documents while xonsh can read/write filesystem and run broad-network shell commands, creating a plausible sensitive-data transfer path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, OCR text, and exposes an MCP server; xonsh can consume stdin/stdout and run shell/Python workflows. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if MinerU output is copied or piped into xonsh, even though no direct shared channel is documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF MinerU output is piped or pasted into xonsh as shell/Python input
IF an MCP or CLI bridge forwards MinerU text into xonsh without sanitization
mitigations: Use a read-only handoff file with no executable syntax
Strip code fences and shell metacharacters before transfer
Disable MCP routes that accept free-form instructions
Review xonsh commands manually before execution
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between MinerU and xonsh

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU reads local PDF/image/DOCX/PPTX/XLSX inputs, and xonsh can read filesystem contents and has broad network egress. If MinerU processes sensitive documents and xonsh later handles the same workspace, leakage to external services or logs is plausible in default use. The pair is not proven isolated, so uncertainty favors medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or document set
IF xonsh forwards file contents to a remote API or logs them
mitigations: Separate workspaces for MinerU and xonsh
Keep sensitive documents out of shared directories
Turn off outbound network calls in xonsh sessions
Redact documents before passing them onward
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: xonsh has filesystem write, shell execution, and subprocess spawning; MinerU exposes APIs/MCP and concurrent inference but no write or shell capability. The main conflict is not symmetric write overlap, but xonsh can mutate shared files that MinerU reads, and MinerU can concurrently process them. Because shared locking is not documented, the safer choice is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or file tree
IF xonsh edits inputs while MinerU is parsing them
mitigations: Use separate input/output directories
Serialize access with a simple lock file
Make MinerU inputs read-only during processing
Avoid concurrent runs on the same workspace
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, formulas, and OCR output; xonsh can execute shell commands and Python expressions. If xonsh treats MinerU output as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect commands or transformations. There is no documented verification step, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF xonsh consumes MinerU extraction output without human review
IF extracted text is used to generate commands or scripts
mitigations: Require manual review before execution
Compare extracted values against source documents
Use dry-run mode for generated commands
Limit xonsh to non-destructive commands during ingestion
requires-engineering: add validation gates before command execution

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. MinerU is positioned as private/offline, while xonsh is a local shell environment with broad egress; that creates a small compliance gap only if regulated data is moved into networked xonsh workflows. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by MinerU and then sent from xonsh to external services
IF retention or logging settings differ across the two workflows
mitigations: Keep regulated data offline in MinerU
Disable external API use in xonsh for regulated datasets
Document a shared retention policy
Review logs for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both tools
